answer: Propose unpaid probation for jetty fire-alert agents: each key labels 100 clips/day for 7 consecutive days, detecting whether a lantern sheds an ember. Auditors assign fresh, disjoint, balanced sets and check hidden labels; below 95 correct/day resets probation and blocks fees. Power recurs; models/hardware are reusable capital; no stake. Shared models and batching lower cost; leaked labels or auditor collusion defeat screening. Ten parallel keys need at least 7,000 clip annotations before fees: this bounds unpaid workload, not dollars or unique owners.
